message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on B&O Railroad in the current auction.

I have $668 and no monopolies. p1 has $824 and is building toward an orange or red monopoly. p2 has $631 and sits on B&O Railroad.

p4 has $270 and two railroads. The auction is at $130 with p2 leading. I will bid around $140 to $160 to block p4 from a cheap third railroad. I need to keep $180 for Tennessee. Dropping is fine if p1 or p2 outbid p4.

p1 raised the bid to $101. p4 still has two railroads and would pay $100 per landing on a third. p2 is bidding $130 despite owning no railroads yet. This suggests p2 may be trying to block p4 or use the property as a trade chip.

Bidding $131 leaves $537. That covers both the $180 Tennessee and $280 Marvin reserves. The earlier plan to cap bids near $140-160 conflicts with this math. p4 only has $270.

p2 is already at $130, which p4 cannot match. p4 has hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic and may need cash for repairs. I am weighing whether to bid $131 or drop.

Bidding $131 forces the other bidders to raise the price. This could drain p4's cash or push p2 and p1 to pay more to block them. I might end up winning the property at a discount. The face value is $200, so $131 to $160 is a good deal.

I own one green property, not a set. The Short Line is still available. Cash is more important than acquiring another railroad.

I now see the full board layout. p1 holds two of three yellows and two of three reds, so he needs Tennessee to complete either set. p2 holds two of three greens and owns the only dark blue pair. p4 has two of three yellows and two railroads, but no monopolies yet.

I have a clear strategic priority list: block p1 from completing the orange set, secure Marvin, prevent p2 from owning Park Place, and keep Electric out of p4's hands.

The current leader is p2 at $130. If I drop now, p4 could still win at $131 and claim a third railroad cheaply. I must stay in to stop that.

p2 explicitly stated he is trying to deny p4. I will bid $140 to keep pressure on p4 while preserving cash for Tennessee and Marvin. I can drop if the price rises above $160.

I will bid the minimum $131 to avoid revealing my ceiling. This forces the other bidders higher while keeping p4's cash drained. I plan a short, quiet message.
